pr.title: Move Field's release source to audiofield/field, and carry existing installs over from okamnesiac/field
pr.head: 91291ec52f8223289a4fde9cbcd964655a1d13c7

summary: A release install is Field installed without a clone. install.sh downloads a tagged source archive from GitHub, builds it under ~/.local/share/field, and writes the repository it came from into a small file, release.conf. field upgrade reads that file to find the newest installer, downloads it, and runs it.

Field's repository moved from okamnesiac/field to audiofield/field. GitHub redirects the old name for now, but okamnesiac/fyra, a private repository, is about to take that name, and that ends the redirect. Both programs put what release.conf recorded ahead of their default, so changing the default alone would leave every existing install asking for a name that then answers 404.

This change makes audiofield/field the default, and it has both programs read a recorded okamnesiac/field as audiofield/field. The installer then writes the new name the next time it installs. A fork's record stays as it is, and an explicit FIELD_REPO still wins.
The code change adds 16 lines across install.sh and src/commands/upgrade.ts. The rest of the diff replaces the old name in the docs and the tests, and adds the two tests that pin the mapping.

cards.title: The move has to happen in order
cards.html:
1. Point field.one at the new name. okamnesiac/audiofield#46 did this, and it is merged.
  2. Release this change, which moves the v0 tag to it.
  3. Rename okamnesiac/fyra to take the old name.

The pull request's check for step 2: after the release, run field upgrade, then head -1 ~/.local/share/field/release.conf. It prints repo=audiofield/field. If it prints repo=okamnesiac/field, do not rename.

groups.title: Where a release comes from
groups.kicker: The default repository changes, and a recorded old name reads as the new one
intro: Two programs decide which repository a release install follows: install.sh, and field upgrade in src/commands/upgrade.ts. They are written in different languages, so each holds its own copy of the name. Both read the same three sources, in this order:

1. FIELD_REPO, when it is set in the environment.
  2. What release.conf recorded, with okamnesiac/field now read as audiofield/field.
  3. The default, now audiofield/field.
The new constant in each program, MOVED_REPO, holds the old name. The comparison is exact, so a fork such as someone/field is untouched.

checks.text: field upgrade and the installer each need the mapping. field upgrade chooses which installer to download, and that installer then reads release.conf again for itself. Because of that split, 0.3.5 can download the new installer through the redirect and still move: the old program needs the old name to resolve, and the new installer does the rest.

files.note: Changes the default, adds MOVED_REPO, and maps a recorded old name in release_init.

checks.text: The installer at this head ran status in a temporary directory against each record. repo=okamnesiac/field printed release audiofield/field v0 is at 0.3.5. repo=someone/field printed a row naming someone/field. repo=okamnesiac/field with FIELD_REPO=someone/field set also named someone/field.

The record moves on any full install. Reading install_release shows that write_record runs on both branches, after a new version and after a repair of the current one. A failed install exits before it, so the old record stays, and the mapping handles it again on the next run.

files.note: The same mapping in releaseSource, which chooses the repository field upgrade and field uninstall download the installer from.

checks.text: upgrade is the only caller of releaseSource, by a search of src and scripts. With the mapping removed from this line, the new test fails with could not download the installer from …/okamnesiac/field/v0/install.sh.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Two new tests pin the mapping, and the rest follow the new default
intro: The test suite serves its own stand-in for GitHub, so the default name appears throughout it. Most of this diff replaces that name. The stand-in now serves only audiofield/field, so an installer that still asked for the old name fails its install in any test that uses the default.

pnpm typecheck is clean, and these four test files pass all 160 tests at 03a1da2. The linux and windows CI jobs pass there too. The one commit after it changes only documentation, so no test here reads anything it changed.

files.note: Adds moves an install that recorded the repository before it moved. The rest replaces the default name.

checks.text: With the mapping removed from install.sh, this test fails on its status row, which reads okamnesiac/field v0 (could not read its version…). So the test catches the regression it is for.

files.note: Adds the same case for field upgrade. The rest replaces the default name.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: Readers learn what an old install or clone needs, and the plan records the decision
intro: docs/install.md now says what to do in each case the move breaks: an old install's field upgrade and field uninstall, an install made with FIELD_DATA_DIR, and an existing clone. It also replaces the old name in its examples. The install plan gains §11, which records why the record moves and the order of the steps. The other files replace the name.

checks.text: A search of the head finds okamnesiac/field in the two MOVED_REPO constants, the two tests that write it into a record, the two paragraphs in docs/install.md that explain the old name, and §1, §10.3, and §11 of the install plan. No workflow or manifest names it.

files.note: New paragraphs under Upgrade a release and in the checkout section say what each old install or clone needs, and Remove a release install names the old versions. The other edits replace the name in examples.

checks.text: The installer at this head ran status offline, piped into bash as this command is, with a ~/ value for FIELD_DATA_DIR. Its row named that directory and it wrote nothing. Bash and zsh both expand the tilde in this position. Without the variable, release_init uses the default data directory, so the sentence above about a second install holds.
The link target #remove-a-release-install matches the heading Remove a release install in this file.

uninstall in src/commands/upgrade.ts calls upgrade, which downloads the installer from the recorded name. So on 0.3.5 and older, field uninstall fails the same way field upgrade does after the rename. Reading the code shows this, and it cannot run until the rename.

install.sh fetches a clone's upstream and compares against it, and it never changes a remote. So this step stays a command the reader runs. The command writes an HTTPS URL, so someone who cloned over SSH substitutes their own form.

files.note: §11 records the move, the order of its steps, and the two things the installer cannot move by itself: field uninstall on old versions, and a clone's origin. §3.2 and §3.3 change to the new name, because they describe the system now.

checks.text: §1 and §10.3 keep the old name on purpose, because they record what was true then. The plan stays at in-progress, and §11 adds no open question.
